items.excerpt: Allie Paschal argues that as AI-generated work floods media, 'creative provenance' — documentation of who made something and how — is becoming essential for designers to rebuild audience trust as the human/AI quality gap narrows.

A hands-on comparison that feeds the exact same prompt into five leading AI UI design tools and compares the generated interfaces — a practical benchmark of where prompt-to-UI quality actually stands in 2026.

A designer/PM-oriented explainer of Model Context Protocol — how MCP servers let AI agents reach design files, docs, and tooling, and what that means for non-engineers. NOTE: MCP angle overlaps with the 07-06 figma-to-code card (explainer, not product news); curator should weigh dedup.
items.notes: Watchlist overlap risk: MCP mentioned in 2026-07-06 figma-to-code card.

items.excerpt: A look at the unglamorous side of AI-powered design systems — governance, drift, and maintenance work that AI generation creates rather than removes — and what design-system teams should prepare for.

Hi3D automates the full pipeline from a text prompt to a print-ready 3D collectible: it generates the model, intelligently splits it into printable parts, adds assembly connectors, and exports files 'in less than five minutes' — no 3D modeling or mesh repair required.

Kyrall launched an AI-automated CAD modeller that turns engineering specifications into parametric 3D models and functional assemblies in minutes, grounded in a 'Context Manager' repository of the user's own design data and best practices.

In its copyright fight with Hollywood, Midjourney is demanding studios disclose their own internal generative-AI use — arguing studios' AI storyboarding experiments show the industry itself trains on unlicensed work. A case whose outcome shapes how designers can legally use image generators.

Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch (v0) says AI building has shifted from prototyping to production, and argues models must be decoupled from agents so teams can swap providers — a stance that directly shapes the design-to-production toolchain designers now rely on.

Google now uses media uploaded through its search tools — images, audio, video — to train its AI models by default; creators who don't want their work in the training set must opt out via Search Services History and Personalization settings. (Same story also on Engadget 07-06.)

Config 2026 session just published to Figma's channel: 'Own the loop: how designers and researchers win with AI evals' — Figma's Setor Zilevu on how design and research teams use AI evaluations to keep quality in the loop.
Config 2026 session: 'Skill issue: how we built an OS for PMs at Figma' — how Figma built PM OS, its internal AI tool for product managers, following the pattern of Ramp's Glass and Stripe's Minions.
Config 2026 session: 'Designing money: how to build a trustworthy brand in the age of AI' ft. Chris Warner — brand design and trust when AI-generated content is everywhere.
